prompt:
Use case: game surface material, reference-driven textured-concept.
Create one square seamless BASE COLOR texture for OLD EXTERIOR LIME PLASTER of the inhabited medieval fantasy houses in the provided reference. This is a FLAT wall surface material to apply to editable 3D meshes, NOT a building, perspective drawing, scene, or presentation.
Material design: weathered pale warm-grey sandy lime plaster, visibly hand-trowelled and uneven, broad irregular patches of coarse aggregate, worn and spalled plaster, scattered shallow crumbling edges exposing darker sandy undercoat, a few small areas of local rough grey-beige fieldstone masonry showing through. About 75% plaster remains intact, 15% exposed sandy undercoat and 10% exposed small stones. The damage comes in uneven organic groups of varied sizes, not evenly spaced spots. A few repaired plaster patches in a slightly different ivory-grey; thin age cracks; soft narrow rain runnels, restrained muted grey-brown accumulated grime. Clear medium-scale mottling and mineral grain that will remain readable when applied to a 3-metre wall rendered only 140 pixels tall. Inhabited, cared-for yet several decades old; substantial crafted tactile texture like the reference. No smooth new paint, no flat clean concrete, no high-gloss/plastic appearance, no black mold blanket, no ruin, no yellow filter.
Style: detailed nostalgic Japanese fantasy RPG hand-painted material, natural earthy restraint, rich tactile surfaces, not a photographic wall or generic noise texture. Uniform frontal orthographic view, no directional illumination, cast shadows or ambient-occlusion painted into the color. All edges tile seamlessly. Edge-to-edge surface only, no doors, windows, beams, foliage, text, border, labels or watermark.
usage: Unlit surface colour on editable 3D facade meshes; final pixels rendered through shared camera and daylight.
